title: Describing
goal: Describe people, places and how you feel, and compare things, using ser, estar, hay and tener.

grammar.p: Use *ser* for what something IS: identity, origin, profession, personality, physical description, time and the date, and where an event takes place (*La fiesta es en mi casa*). Use *estar* for WHERE something is and HOW someone is right now: location, health, mood, temporary states (*Estoy cansado. El hospital está en el centro.*). Some adjectives change meaning: *es aburrido* (he's boring) vs *está aburrido* (he's bored); *es listo* (he's clever) vs *está listo* (he's ready).
ex: Mi esposa es de Puebla y es enfermera.
My wife is from Puebla and she's a nurse.
Hoy está muy cansada.
Today she's very tired.
¿Dónde está la farmacia?
Where is the pharmacy?

grammar.p: *Hay* never changes: *hay un baño* (there is a bathroom), *hay tres farmacias* (there are three pharmacies). Use *hay* to say something EXISTS, usually with *un/una*, a number, *mucho/poco* or no article. Use *estar* to say where a specific, known thing is: *Hay una farmacia en la esquina* vs *La farmacia está en la esquina*.
ex: ¿Hay un baño por aquí?
Is there a bathroom around here?
Hay mucha gente en la sala de espera.
There are a lot of people in the waiting room.
El baño está al fondo.
The bathroom is at the back.

grammar.p: Spanish says you HAVE hunger, thirst, cold, fear: *tener hambre, sed, frío, calor, sueño, miedo, prisa, razón* and age: *tener … años*. Never use *estar* or *ser* with these. To say 'very', use *mucho/mucha*, not *muy*, and match the noun: *mucha hambre, mucha sed* (feminine) but *mucho frío, mucho calor, mucho sueño, mucho miedo* (masculine).
ex: Tengo mucha hambre.
I'm very hungry.
Mi hijo tiene miedo de los perros.
My son is afraid of dogs.
¿Cuántos años tiene su papá?
How old is your father?

grammar.p: Adjectives match the noun in gender and number and usually go after it: *una casa pequeña, unos doctores simpáticos*. Most adjectives ending in *-e* or a consonant change only for number: *grande → grandes, difícil → difíciles*. Possessives go before the noun and agree with the THING owned: *mi/mis, tu/tus, su/sus, nuestro/nuestra/nuestros/nuestras*. *Su* can mean his, her, your (usted), your (ustedes) or their; add *de él, de ella* if it's unclear.
ex: Las enfermeras son muy amables.
The nurses are very kind.
Señora, ¿cómo se llama su hijo?
Ma'am, what's your son's name?
Nuestra casa es pequeña, pero nuestros vecinos son simpáticos.
Our house is small, but our neighbors are nice.

grammar.p: *más … que* (more … than), *menos … que* (less … than), *tan … como* (as … as). Irregular: *mejor* (better), *peor* (worse), *mayor* (older), *menor* (younger) — never *más mejor*. After *que* use *yo* and *tú*: *más alto que yo*. *Muy* goes before adjectives and adverbs and never changes (*muy cansado*). *Mucho* after a verb doesn't change (*trabajo mucho*); before a noun it agrees (*mucha gente, muchos pacientes*). *Poco* works the same way (*poca gente*).
ex: Mi hermano es mayor que yo.
My brother is older than me.
Este café es mejor que el otro.
This coffee is better than the other one.
Mi papá es tan alto como yo.
My dad is as tall as I am.

phrases: Is there a bathroom around here?
Es más caro que el otro.
It's more expensive than the other one.
Mi hermano es mayor que yo.
My brother is older than me.
There are a lot of people.

items.why: Origin → ser: es de Puebla.

items.q: El hospital ___ en la calle Harrison.
items.qen: The hospital is on Harrison Street.
items.why: Location of a specific place → estar: está.

items.q: ___ tres farmacias cerca de mi casa.
items.qen: There are three pharmacies near my house.
items.why: Saying something exists (with a number) → hay, which never changes.
hijas is feminine plural → simpáticas.
With tener expressions 'very' = mucho/mucha, agreeing with the noun; hambre is feminine → mucha.
Health / temporary condition → estar.

items.q: Mi hermano tiene 40 años y yo tengo 45. Él es ___ que yo.
items.qen: My brother is 40 and I'm 45. He is ___ than me.
items.why: He is younger → menor.

items.q: How do you say: "I'm afraid of dogs."
items.why: Fear is a tener expression: tener miedo de…

items.q: Mi hijo no tiene nada que hacer. ___ aburrido.
items.qen: My son has nothing to do. He's bored.
items.why: Bored (a temporary state) → está aburrido. Es aburrido would mean he's a boring person.
Time uses ser; with singular hora → ¿Qué hora es?
más … que = more … than.

items.q: Mi hermano es tan alto ___ mi papá.
items.qen: My brother is as tall as my dad.
items.why: tan … como = as … as.

items.q: Este restaurante es ___ que el otro.
items.qen: This restaurant is better than the other one.
items.why: Better = mejor (never más mejor); singular subject → mejor.
With usted, 'your' = su (singular because hijo is singular).

items.qen: Ana and her sister are nurses.
items.why: Profession → ser; two people → son.

items.qen: Is there a bathroom around here?
items.why: Asking whether something exists (un baño) → hay.

items.qen: Pablo works a lot; he's always tired.
items.why: After a verb, 'a lot' = mucho, which doesn't change.

items.q: Hay ___ gente en el parque hoy.
items.qen: There are a lot of people in the park today.
items.why: gente is a feminine singular noun → mucha gente.

items.q: You want to know what your friend's wife is like (personality, looks). You ask: "¿___ es tu esposa?"
items.why: What is someone like? = ¿Cómo es…? (¿Cómo está…? would ask how she's doing.)
The possessive agrees with the thing owned: abuelos is masculine plural → nuestros.

items.en: My parents are from Guatemala.
items.why: Origin → ser; ellos → son.

items.en: Where is the bathroom?
items.why: Location → estar: está.

items.en: My daughter is ten years old.
items.why: Age uses tener: tiene diez años.

items.en: The nurses are very kind.
items.why: Adjectives ending in -e only add -s for plural: amables.

items.q: Yo ___ más alto que mi papá.
items.en: I'm taller than my dad.
items.why: Physical description → ser; yo → soy.

items.q: Hoy ___ muy nerviosa por el examen.
items.en: Today I'm very nervous about the exam.
items.why: A feeling right now → estar; yo → estoy.

items.q: En mi calle ___ dos restaurantes mexicanos.
items.en: On my street there are two Mexican restaurants.
items.why: There is / there are = hay (never changes).

items.en: —Are you cold? —Yes, I'm very cold.
items.why: With tener expressions 'very' = mucho/mucha; frío is masculine → mucho.

items.q: Mi casa es ___ grande como tu casa.
items.en: My house is as big as your house.
items.why: tan … como = as … as.

items.q: Este hospital es ___ que el otro.
items.en: This hospital is better than the other one.
items.why: Better = mejor (never más bueno or más mejor in this sense).

items.en: Sir, what is your wife's name?
items.why: With usted, 'your' = su.

items.en: The tacos are very tasty.
items.why: Taste of food → estar rico; los tacos is masculine plural → ricos.

items.en: I'm hungry; is there anything to eat?
items.why: Hungry = tener hambre.

items.en: The clinic is closed on Sundays.
items.why: Open/closed is a state → estar: está cerrada.

items.en: My husband is a doctor.
items.why: Profession → ser (and no article: es doctor).

items.q: La fiesta ___ en mi casa el sábado.
items.en: The party is at my house on Saturday.
items.why: Where an EVENT takes place → ser: la fiesta es en mi casa.

items.en: This medicine is very expensive.
items.why: medicina is feminine singular → cara.

items.q: Mi hermano es ___ que yo; él tiene 30 años y yo tengo 35.
items.en: My brother is younger than me; he's 30 and I'm 35.
items.why: Younger = menor (más joven is also correct).

items.q: Hay ___ pacientes hoy; la clínica está llena.
items.en: There are a lot of patients today; the clinic is full.
items.why: Before a noun, mucho agrees: pacientes is masculine plural → muchos.

items.en: We're in a hurry.
items.why: In a hurry = tener prisa; nosotros → tenemos.

items.title: Describing your family to a friend

opts: Está alta, muy simpática y le encanta bailar.
Es alta, muy simpática y le encanta bailar.
Es alto, muy simpático y le encanta bailar.
turns.why: Description → ser; esposa is feminine → alta, simpática.

opts: Es de Ohio, pero su familia es de México.
Está de Ohio, pero su familia es de México.
Es de Ohio, pero tu familia es de México.
turns.why: Origin → ser; 'her family' = su familia (tu familia would mean Lucía's family).

turns.en: Nice! And do you have kids?

opts: Sí, tienen dos. La mayor tiene diez años.
Sí, tenemos dos. La mayor es diez años.
Sí, tenemos dos. La mayor tiene diez años.
turns.why: My wife and I → tenemos; age uses tener: tiene diez años.

turns.en: Come on in. Do you want something to drink? Are you thirsty?

turns.why: Thirsty = tener sed; sed is feminine → mucha sed.

turns.es: Claro, hay agua y limonada. Oye, la ventana está abierta. ¿Tienes frío?
turns.en: Sure, there's water and lemonade. Hey, the window is open. Are you cold?

opts: Sí, estoy un poco de frío.
Sí, tengo un poco de frío.
turns.why: Being cold = tener frío; 'a little' with a noun = un poco de.

turns.en: No problem. Do you want a blanket?

turns.es: Buenas tardes. ¿En qué le puedo ayudar?
turns.en: Good afternoon. How can I help you?

turns.why: Location of a specific place → estar: ¿Dónde está…?

turns.es: Está en el primer piso, al lado de la cafetería.
turns.en: It's on the first floor, next to the cafeteria.

turns.why: Asking whether one exists (un baño) → hay.

turns.es: Sí, hay uno enfrente de la farmacia.
turns.en: Yes, there's one across from the pharmacy.

turns.es: ¿Qué departamento prefieres, el del centro o el de Evanston?
turns.en: Which apartment do you prefer, the one downtown or the one in Evanston?

opts: El del centro es más caro como el de Evanston, pero es más bonito.
El del centro es más caro que el de Evanston, pero es más bonito.
El del centro es más cara que el de Evanston, pero es más bonita.
turns.why: más … que; departamento is masculine → caro, bonito.

opts: El de Evanston es más grande, pero el del centro es mejor.
El de Evanston es más grande, pero el del centro es más mejor.
El de Evanston es más grandes, pero el del centro es mejor.
turns.why: Better = mejor (never más mejor); grande stays singular for one apartment.

opts: No, soy enfermo. Me duele la garganta y tengo fiebre.
No, estoy enfermo. Me duele la garganta y tengo fiebre.
No, estoy enfermo. Me duele la garganta y estoy fiebre.
turns.why: Being sick is a condition → estar; fever is a tener expression: tengo fiebre.

turns.es: Ay, lo siento. ¿Y quién está con tus hijos hoy?
turns.en: Oh, I'm sorry. And who is with your kids today?

opts: Mi esposa es con ellos. Hoy no trabaja.
Mi esposa hay con ellos. Hoy no trabaja.
Mi esposa está con ellos. Hoy no trabaja.
turns.why: Being with someone (location) → estar: está con ellos.

turns.es: Mucho gusto. Soy la mamá de Carlos.
turns.en: Nice to meet you. I'm Carlos's mom.

opts: Mucho gusto, señora. Tu hijo es muy simpático.
Mucho gusto, señora. Su hijo es muy simpático.
Mucho gusto, señora. Su hijo son muy simpáticos.
turns.why: With an older person you've just met → usted, so 'your' = su; one son → es simpático.

turns.es: Gracias. ¿Usted también es doctor, como Carlos?
turns.en: Thank you. Are you a doctor too, like Carlos?

turns.es: ¡Qué bien! ¿Y su familia vive aquí en Chicago?
turns.en: How nice! And does your family live here in Chicago?

opts: Mi esposa y yo vivimos aquí, pero mis padres son en Michigan.
Mi esposa y yo vivimos aquí, pero mis padres hay en Michigan.
Mi esposa y yo vivimos aquí, pero mis padres están en Michigan.
turns.why: Location of people → estar: están en Michigan.

roleplay.title: Describing your families
roleplay.setup: You're having coffee with a coworker who is becoming a friend. Describe your family to her and find out about hers: what they're like, how old they are, where they are, and how they're doing.
roleplay.persona: You are Gabriela Hernández, 38, a hospital pharmacist from San Salvador, El Salvador, living in Chicago. Your husband, Julio, is a teacher; he's tall, funny and very patient. You have two kids: Sofía (12), who is very smart and loves soccer, and Mateo (7), who is shy and afraid of dogs. Your mother lives in San Salvador; she's 70 and in good health, but this week she's a little sick (a cold) and you are worried. You are the youngest of four siblings. Use tú with the learner. Speak only in the present tense, in short, simple sentences, using ser, estar, hay, tener (age, miedo, etc.), adjectives and comparisons (más…que, tan…como, mayor/menor). Share details only when asked, and ask the learner about his family too. If the learner makes a ser/estar mistake, keep going and use the correct form naturally in your reply.
roleplay.opening: ¡Por fin un café! Oye, nunca hablamos de la familia. ¿Cómo es tu familia?
goals: Describe one family member's looks and personality with ser and correctly agreeing adjectives
Ask how old her children are
Find out where her mother is and how she is doing (estar)
Make at least two comparisons (más…que, tan…como, mayor/menor)
Use a tener expression (miedo, hambre, sueño…) at least once

roleplay.title: Looking at apartments
roleplay.setup: You're looking at two apartments with the building manager, an older man. Use usted. Find out what each one has, where things are, and which one is better for you.
roleplay.persona: You are Don Raúl Castillo, 63, building manager from Monterrey, Mexico. You show two apartments in a building in Logan Square. Apartment 2A: two bedrooms, big, very bright, faces the street (a little noisy), 1,900 dollars a month. Apartment 4B: one bedroom, smaller, very quiet, has a new kitchen, 1,500 dollars a month. Both are near the Blue Line; the train station is two blocks away. There is a laundry room in the basement and an elevator; there is no parking, but there is a garage across the street. The building is old but very clean. Use usted with the learner. Speak only in the present tense, in simple sentences, using ser, estar, hay and comparisons. Answer only what is asked; if the learner asks which one is better, ask what is more important to him.
roleplay.opening: Buenas tardes. Pase, por favor. Este es el departamento 2A. Es grande, ¿verdad?
goals: Ask what there is in each apartment (hay)
Ask where the train station and the laundry room are (estar)
Compare the two apartments using más…que, menos…que or tan…como
Ask how much each one costs
Use usted throughout and say which apartment you prefer and why (porque)
